levels.name: Dewdrop First Turn
levels.hint: Tap the empty axle, then tap a gear in the tray. Gears must touch to pass the turn on.

levels.name: Pebble Path
levels.hint: Two gears pass motion along. The one next to the motor decides which way everything turns.

levels.name: Little Lantern
levels.hint: Teeth must meet: neighbouring gears need tooth counts that add up to 24.

levels.name: Mossy Milestone
levels.hint: Follow the chain from the motor to the windmill. Every shaft on the way needs a gear.

levels.name: Fern Fitting
levels.hint: A gear two axles away can only reach through the axle between them.

levels.name: Clover Crank
levels.hint: Look at the axle beside the motor first — its size is forced by the gear already bolted there.

levels.name: Puddle Pinion
levels.hint: The garden only wakes when every objective is met. Press RUN to test your build.

levels.name: Snail Street
levels.hint: The tray shows what you have. You never need every piece.

levels.name: Acorn Assembly
levels.hint: Undo is free and always available. Experiment, then step back.

levels.name: Buttercup Bench
levels.hint: Direction changes at every mesh: clockwise becomes anti-clockwise.

levels.name: Wheelbarrow Walk
levels.hint: A longer train does not change the output speed by itself — the end gears decide.

levels.name: Rain Barrel
levels.hint: If the motor turns one way, count the meshes to the mechanism.

levels.name: Trellis Turn
levels.hint: Shafts can bend: follow the pegs around the corner.

levels.name: Herb Spiral
levels.hint: The same gear can serve a different purpose in a different garden. Read the objective.

levels.name: Greenhouse Nook
levels.hint: Try the largest gear first when you need a slower mechanism.

levels.name: Twine and Timber
levels.hint: A mechanism that needs half speed wants a driven gear twice the size of the driver.

levels.name: Copper Kettle
levels.hint: The ratio label on the objective tells you exactly what the motor must deliver.

levels.name: Fernery Fork
levels.hint: Two mechanisms can share one motor. Both need power.

levels.name: Twin Watering Cans
levels.hint: Each branch has its own tooth pattern. Solve one side at a time.

levels.name: Petal Press
levels.hint: Watch the axle count on each branch: direction depends on how many meshes the power crosses.

levels.name: Copper Cup
levels.hint: A belt can reach a shaft that gears cannot. Open belts keep the direction.

levels.name: Winding Creek
levels.hint: A crossed belt reverses the turn without adding a gear.

levels.name: Two Storeys
levels.hint: Two gears on one axle turn together. That is how power climbs to the upper layer.

levels.name: Upper Orchard
levels.hint: Upper-layer gears only mesh with other upper-layer gears.

levels.name: Clutch and Clover
levels.hint: A clutch must be engaged before its shaft passes power. Tap the clutch lever, then RUN.
